name: STA Email 02 - the baby aisle
subject: The bottle in the baby aisle nobody pulled
preview: You did everything right. That was never the problem.
html:
You bought it because your mother used it on you.

That is not carelessness. That is trust, and it was earned over sixty years of advertising built to earn it.

Johnson & Johnson paid $5.5 billion to settle roughly 76,000 baby powder claims. They tried three separate times to move the whole thing into a shell company so it would never reach a jury. Three times. That is not what innocent looks like.

They pulled it off American shelves in 2020. Off every shelf on earth by 2023. And the whole time, they said it was fine.

Walmart stocked it. Target stocked it. CVS stocked it. They watched the verdicts roll in for ten years and kept it in the baby aisle, right beside the diapers, exactly where a new mother reaches.

You were never careless. You were sold to.

Tonight, one thing

Pick the one cleaner you use most, the one that touches the floor your kids and your dog live on. If the company will not print what is in it before anybody makes them, do not buy that one again.

You do not have to guess which ones. The scan walks your house room by room and tells you exactly what is worth dealing with first. Three minutes.

name: STA Email 03 - the eczema that will not clear
subject: Her skin will not clear and you have tried everything
preview: Before you buy another cream, rule this out.
html:
You have bought the cream. Twice.

The patches come back anyway. Behind the knees, inside the elbows, the same spots. The doctor says it is eczema and to keep it moisturised, and you do, and it comes back.

Nobody has asked you what you wash her sheets in.

She spends eight hours a night in that fabric. Skin to cotton, every night, for her whole childhood. It is the longest exposure in your house and it is the one nobody thinks to look at.

New York State had to pass a law capping 1,4-dioxane in cleaning products before the manufacturers reformulated. It is not on the ingredient list. It is not an ingredient. It is a byproduct of how detergent gets made, so nobody has to declare it.

The thing hurting her was never going to be printed on the box.

Tonight, one thing

Run your next load on an extra rinse. One button, costs nothing. If her skin settles over the next week, you have your answer about what is sitting in the fabric.

name: STA Email 04 - the headache at the sink
subject: If you get a headache doing dishes, read this
preview: It is not you being sensitive.
html:
Your hands crack and never quite heal.

And there is a headache that shows up while you are standing at the sink, and lifts about twenty minutes after you walk away from it.

You have probably decided you are just sensitive. You are not. You are having a reaction to something you are not allowed to read.

One word on that bottle is doing a lot of work: fragrance. Under US labelling rules it is a trade secret. A company can put hundreds of separate chemicals behind that single word and never name one of them.

So when you turn the bottle over, you are not reading an ingredient list. You are reading the parts they agreed to tell you about.

And dish soap touches every single thing that goes in your family's mouth. Every plate, every fork, every cup. A film stays on the dish. You are not tasting it. You are eating it.

Tonight, one thing

Open the cupboard under your sink and count how many bottles say fragrance or parfum. Just count. Most women get to four or five and stop.

That number is the size of what you have not been told. The scan counts it for you, room by room, and tells you which one to deal with first.

name: STA Email 05 - the tight chest
subject: That tight chest after you mop is not in your head
preview: 37 million bottles. You never heard a word.
html:
You clean the house and then you cannot take a full breath.

It passes. You open a window, you get on with the day, and you file it under being run down. It happens again next week.

Your body is reporting something and you have been taught to overrule it.

In October 2022, Clorox recalled around 37 million bottles of scented Pine-Sol for bacterial contamination. Thirty seven million. Of a product sold to you as the thing that kills germs.

Did you hear about it? Almost nobody did. It ran for a day and vanished, while that bottle sat under sinks in millions of houses, being used on counters and floors and, in plenty of homes, on the high chair tray.

The company selling you protection could not keep its own bottles clean, and the system that is supposed to warn you barely made a sound. You are not being protected. You are being marketed to.

Tonight, one thing

Use the floor cleaner where your kids play one more time and pay attention to your chest. Then believe your body over the label.

name: STA Email 06 - the cough that only happens indoors
subject: The cough that only shows up indoors
preview: You are not cleaning the air. You are adding to it.
html:
Somebody in your house coughs at night and never during the day.

Or there is a headache that lifts the moment you open a window. Or the asthma is worse in winter, when the house is shut.

You have blamed the season. Look at what is plugged into the wall.

Air freshener does not remove anything. There is nothing in a can of fresh linen that finds a bad smell and takes it away. It coats the inside of your nose and lays a stronger smell over a weaker one. The original is still there. Now you are breathing both, plus whatever carried it.

And you breathe it in the smallest, least ventilated rooms you own. The bathroom. The car. The bedroom, for eight hours, while she sleeps.

I have never had a plug-in in my home. Not because I read a study. Because I could not make peace with making a room smell like something that does not grow anywhere.

Tonight, one thing

Unplug the one in the bedroom. That is eight hours of breathing you get back for free. If you want the house to smell like something, put a pot on the stove with orange peel and a cinnamon stick.

CHECK THE AIR IN MY HOUSE

name: STA Email 07 - the high chair tray
subject: You are spraying a pesticide on the high chair
preview: That is not an insult. That is the paperwork.
html:
You wipe the high chair tray before every meal.

Because that is what a good mother does. Then you put food on it.

Disinfectant sprays are registered with the EPA as pesticides. That is not me being dramatic, that is the regulatory category. A product whose job is to kill living things is a pesticide, licensed as one, with a registration number printed on the can.

The label says ventilate. Nobody ventilates. You spray the bathroom and shut the door, because that is the entire point of cleaning the bathroom.

Here is the part that matters. Most of what you wipe down every day does not need a pesticide. It needs soap and a cloth. Killing 99.9 percent of germs on a counter that was not making anyone sick is a marketing achievement, not a health one.

Tonight, one thing

Pick one surface you disinfect out of habit rather than need. The kitchen table, probably. Soap and water this week instead. Nobody gets sick, and that is one less exposure a day for everyone in the house.

name: STA Email 08 - twelve hours on your eyes
subject: Twelve hours a day, on the thinnest skin you have
preview: And most of them do not list it.
html:
It is the one thing you are not willing to give up.

I know. It is tied to how you feel walking out the door, and I am not going to pretend that is nothing.

But it sits closest to your eyes, on the thinnest skin on your body, for twelve hours a day, most days, for decades.

Researchers at Notre Dame tested more than 200 North American cosmetics and found the marker for PFAS, the forever chemicals, in 82 percent of waterproof mascaras and 63 percent of foundations. Most of those products did not list them.

The reason a mascara survives a workday, a cry and a swim is often a class of chemicals built not to break down. That is the feature. That is also the problem, because your body clears them over years, not days.

Tonight, one thing

You do not have to throw out your makeup bag. Pick the product that sits on you longest, usually foundation, and make that the first one you replace when it runs out. One product. Not the bag.

name: STA Email 09 - the lunch you reheat
subject: Do not microwave the bag
preview: The cheapest fix of the whole month.
html:
You are running late, so the lunch goes in the microwave in the bag.

Everybody does it. I am not going to make you feel bad about it. I am going to give you thirty seconds of information that changes it for good.

Heat is what moves chemicals out of plastic and into food. Not time on the shelf. Not the plastic sitting in a drawer. Heat, fat and acid, and a microwave hands you all three at once. A hot bag, a greasy sauce, a tomato.

So it is the leftovers you reheat in the container, the vegetables you steam in the pouch, the lunch you warm in the bag. Those are the moments. Not the drawer.

Tonight, one thing

Move the food onto a plate or into a glass dish before it goes in. That is it. No shopping, nothing thrown away, no budget. One extra dish to wash, and you have removed a daily exposure for your whole family starting with dinner tonight.

If you do nothing else I suggest this month, do this one.

name: STA Email 10 - you paid extra for the healthy one
subject: You paid extra for the healthy oil
html:
You buy the expensive one because it is the healthy one.

That is the whole reason it is in your cart. You are paying a premium to do right by your family and you have never once been given a way to check.

UC Davis has tested avocado oil more than once now, and the answer keeps coming back the same. A large share of the bottles on American shelves are rancid before you open them, or cut with cheaper oil, or both.

You are paying a premium price and getting neither.

Let me be precise, because this gets said badly all over the internet. Olive oil is not a seed oil. My problem is not botany. My problem is that you cannot verify what is in the bottle, there is no meaningful enforcement of the label, and rancid fat tastes fine once it is cooked into something.

Tonight, one thing

Smell your cooking oil. Right at the neck of the bottle. If it smells like crayons, or old nuts, or nothing at all, it has turned. Five seconds, costs nothing. Then cook with beef tallow, which is stable at heat and which you can actually see.

name: STA Email 11 - you cannot read your way out
subject: You cannot read your way out of this
preview: And that was never your failure.
html:
You have stood in an aisle turning a bottle over, trying to do the right thing.

Everybody in this business tells you to read the label. I am going to tell you something else.

It would not have saved you.

In 2021, Procter & Gamble recalled aerosol antiperspirants and body sprays after benzene was found in them. Benzene is a known human carcinogen. It was not an ingredient. Nobody put it in on purpose. It came out of the process.

No amount of careful reading in that aisle would have caught it. The recalls arrive after the years of use, not before, and when they arrive they arrive quietly.

You cannot read your way out of this. That is not your failure, it is the design.

So here is what I actually want for you. Not a cupboard cleared out over a weekend. A different supply chain. Products where somebody puts their name on what is in it, before anyone makes them.

That is why Switch to America exists. We are a new supply chain, built on family values, trust and affordability. We cannot stop them. I stopped expecting to. But we can stop walking into their stores.
